I don’t know if I did the bisect thing right, but compiling one commit before #99538 the test project still works, but not on that PR (build a3525bc). Hope I did it right.

A bit of history about this test project: for [more than a year](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/82642#issuecomment-1822859656) it was used to test several LightmapGI bugs like light probes not working, large lightmaps bug, and I accumulated the tested bugs on each interaction so it tests multiple past issues at once. I’ve recently changed to a simpler test but it seems like this old monstrosity is still needed.

About the current issue, I tried clean all the light probes, addons and reduce the lightmap size but the crash persists on #99538.

Another interesting issue is that it crashes on the first time the project is opened, but if I insist a few times it freezes the PC for a while but complete the baking after several minutes, a way longer than previews commits.

This project has hundreds of trees with transparent materials set to “Alpha Scissor”. Maybe there’s something with this mode.

Edit: 
My system info: `Godot v4.4.dev (a3525bc01) - Windows 10.0.22631 - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6614) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-12700KF (20 threads)`

Edit 2: By turning off the transparency on the leaves material (`res://DemoScene/Trees/leaves.tres`) the terrain bakes normally but the tunnel doesn't receive shadowmasks anymore (It was working normally on the Shasowmasks PR). The the terrain has local UVs, but tunnel have both UV1 and UV2 imported from Blender.

I can't reproduce this on 4.4.dev d33da79d3f8fe84be2521d25b9ba8e440cf25a88 with the MRP. I suspect another out-of-VRAM situation like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/95204. Shadowmasks are working, although they look broken within the tunnel (i.e. the interior of the tunnel isn't shadowed in the shadowmask in most parts of it):

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67ee1891-d3eb-4fc1-9dac-dced2dd02f73)

When baking lightmaps in the MRP, system VRAM utilization tops out at 9.1 GB (but depending on other programs running on the system, it could exceed 10 GB).

The GPU VRAM peaked at about 80% before the crash.

[transparency_crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18446185/transparency_crash.zip)

And after a bit to digging around, it seems my editor will crash if there are more than exactly 14 trees in the scene. Very strange.

If no one else is having this issue, it might as well be a driver issue. I haven't updated my nvidea drivers for over a year now.
I also run a windows 10 v1803 because I don't have enough C drive space to update it anymore.

I don't think is your system. Considering that I have 12GB of VRAM and the original scene peaks at only 9, maybe there is a short burst of huge vram usage that is not detected by debuggers. Probably somewhere around the "plot direct lightnig" phase (or the beginning of the next phase) because the crash is consistently on the same spot.

Today I installed beta1 and I encountered similar issue. I have quite complex 3d scene and my GPU has 8GB of VRAM. Looking at graphs in Windows task manager  it seems that I don't go over the limit, but maybe task manager is not showing fast peaks. I don't have any issues in 4.4alpha7. I have an AMD card and baking sometimes work, but its at least 3 times slower than in alpha. When it crash though, I receive a popup with driver timeout issue.

I tried but can't reproduce it either (i tried all linked projects and none would crash). I limited my VRAM to 8GB on Linux (`amdgpu.vramlimit=8192` kernel parameter) and the lightmapping completed fine - this was not the case when i tried the other issue about VRAM usage during lightmapping Calinou linked (which crashed as expected). According to amdgpu_top Godot itself never went above around 6ish GB of VRAM with the original MRP, so i don't think the culprit is a sudden short spike.

It has been a few weeks since i last looked at the lightmapper code but IIRC a problem it has when it comes to VRAM utilization is that it preallocates pretty much everything it needs, so there shouldn't really be any spiking (at least none that Godot directly controls) above that 6ish GB VRAM. Also https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/99538 doesn't seem to allocate more VRAM during lightmapping (i did a quick check of the changes) than before (which didn't crash) so i think there is something different going on than using too much VRAM.

System info: Godot v4.4.beta (7b1ed520b) - openSUSE Tumbleweed 20250108 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (RADV NAVI31) - AMD Ryzen 7 3700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) (also 24GB VRAM for the GPU, limited to 8GB via kernel parameter and 32GB of system RAM)

Unfortunately, I can't reproduce the crash either, but I can remember that I encountered this crash at some point during development. However, it was suddenly gone (without any relevant change) so I thought it was fixed by a driver update.
To those who can: Could you retest with max transparency rays set to 1 or 2 (project setting)?

Using the latest master I still crash.

The crash seems to happen on lightmapper_rd.cpp when p_step_function is called for **"Integrate indirect lighting"**.
I've also had it crash on rd->sync() a bit further inside the compute shader on the ray_iterations loop when I removed the progress window.

I believe this might be some edge case on the vulkan's end that might have been fixed on newer versions.
Can someone who has this crash **share what's your vulkan driver** version?

Mine's a bit outdated Vulkan Instance Version 1.3.236 .... on Win10, Nvidea 1070
(you can get this by running 'vulkaninfo' on windows)

**Edit: Updated to the latest Nvidea drivers, Vulkan ver: 1.3.290**
**Still crashing**.
In my case, I crash even if I set the transparency rays to 1.
I tried setting all possible options of low settings and ray numbers, but still crashes on the original MRP.

I also tried the [transparency_crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18446185/transparency_crash.zip) MRP (which should use only 6GB VRAM)
But weirdly enough, now it goes past the Indirect light and crashes on when the progress message is at the "Denoising" step.
And if I disable "Denoising" on the lightmapperGI node it works.

So I think the driver update seems to fix some things:
- I think the original MRP might be crashing because of lack a VRAM (need 9.1 and I have 8)
- The 6GB transparency_crash project AND the 15-tree's min-crash project is now crashing on the denoise and is another problem?

Edit: Fun note, I had to revert the newest Nvidea driver update because it caused my windows to constantly BSOD on my very old computer.

@SpockBauru Could you create a new issue for the lightning regression (in the tunnel)?

I investigated the issue (using the lightmap debug textures) and saw that the lightmap UV2 albedo and emission textures don't match the rest (position/normal/etc.). By that I mean the scale/position in the texture as well as individual UV2 islands for some reason. (needs more digging)
I can reproduce this in 4.3 by adding emission to the surface materials of the tunnel. It looks like this has been an unnoticed problem for a long time and after transparency support got added it became much more noticeable because we actually check for surface transparency when tracing rays (not just any hits). The albedo texture is transparent at the parts where no polygon (in UV2) is located.
In the shader those textured are sampled the exact same way, so most of the surface becomes transparent.

> [@SpockBauru](https://github.com/SpockBauru) Could you create a new issue for the lightning regression (in the tunnel)?

Done, opened an issue for the tunnel regression in #102164. I've made a new MRP with the bare minimum to reproduce the issue.

Can you try a smaller region setting (must be a power of two, e.g. 128, 256, 512, etc) in Project Settings (advanced settings must be enabled at the top right corner of the settings window):

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e91b26f-78dd-488c-b0f6-da4fe599398b)

The crash might be due to a GPU timeout that Windows forces for compute shaders that the new functionality cause the compute shader to exceed (and if this is the case it'd be Linux users weren't able to reproduce this crash). That the crash happens inside the driver for both Nvidia and AMD users and that it takes more time to calculate the lightmaps even when it doesn't crash also hints towards this being the case.

The region setting mentioned above will try to use more partial invocations for the compute shader - it is only for indirect lighting but that is the slowest part of the lightmapping process, though it wouldn't help if it still happens during the other parts. After https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102243 is merged, enabling low VRAM mode and making sure the lightmap array uses more than one slice should also help as that'd split the shader invocations further for all passes (currently it wouldn't make a difference because the MRP uses a lightmap array with only a single gigantic slice - i think splitting the terrain to multiple individual meshes so that a texture size smaller than 8192 could be used would help a lot here).

Just tested on Windows, I can confirm the crash. It happens during the direct lighting pass which is why the region size has no effect. I think this is pretty clearing a TDR caused by the extra rays cast during direct lighting. It needs to render in regions like indirect lighting does

So I came to similar conclusion that direct lightning step is an issue. There are also few other observations that I made, that are not necessary relevant to transparency PR:
1.  Numbers of lights set to be baked is heavily impacting this step. Each one is adding one `trace_direct_light` call. My recommendation for more complex scenes is to only bake one light. This probably should also be split similarly to ray count.
2. `light angular distance` / `light size` is very heavily impacting this step too. It seems that this is introducing multiple loops in shader when enabled. By multiple I mean really a lot. I think its something around `bake_params.transparency_rays * params.ray_count / AA_SAMPLES`. This setting is instantly killing my bakes on more complex scenes. 
3. Recently added anti aliasing is introducing additional loops even when angular distance is set to 0. That might not be a problem with simple scenes but seems like the more complex the scenes the more expensive `trace_ray` call is becoming. 
4. None of the editor settings is actually affecting the performance of single thread in direct pass light step. So there is not really an editor setting that we can use to workaround this issue by changing properties of lightmapper itself.

I am not expert here so I could made some wrong assumptions, but hope someone with more experience will find something useful in my observations.
